branches.destination: takes the source heap buffer, size, and capacity
branches.name: heap_source
branches.source_when_destination_heap: takes the destination's old heap buffer and capacity; that buffer keeps its bytes except byte 0, set to NUL; size 0
branches.source_when_destination_inline_or_null: becomes an empty inline string: pointer becomes its own +0x10 address, size 0, byte 0 of its inline buffer NUL; the destination's old inline bytes are abandoned, nothing freed

branches.destination: keeps its own buffer and capacity; source bytes copied in; size becomes the source size; NUL written just past the copied bytes
branches.fast_paths: empty source writes only the NUL; one-byte source uses a single load/store with the same effect; longer sources use memcpy
branches.fit_note: always fits a live destination: an inline source holds at most 15 bytes and every live destination buffer holds at least 16
branches.name: inline_source_copy
branches.source: left empty: size 0, byte 0 of its inline buffer NUL, pointer and capacity unchanged

branches.condition: destination object is the source object
branches.effect: the string is emptied: size 0 and byte 0 NUL, pointer and capacity unchanged; a null pointer becomes the inline buffer address first
branches.name: self_move
branches.note: holds on every self path, heap and inline alike, as traced; recorded, not smoothed over

callers.note: caller semantics beyond addresses and FDE ranges are not claimed

calls.allocates_or_frees: none; heap buffers only change owners

layout.inline_rule: pointer equals the object's own +0x10 address

routine.arguments: destination string object in rdi, source string object in rsi
